checks.label: All the entries in the second row relate to the second equation: wherever equations become a grid, each equation fills its own row in order, and a row read back gives its equation again

A matrix times a column vector is a linear combination of the columns of the matrix: for every pair of whole amounts from none to three and every tip on the paper, the chain of columns, nose to tail, ends where the rows add up to
[V] = [R] × [I], where [I] is the list of currents to be found: the loops' resistance grid times the loop currents gives the column of voltages, and those voltages make both loop equations true

Every worked number is right: row 2, column 1 of [4 7 1; 2 5 3] is 2; [1 3; 2 1] times (2, 1) is (5, 5), through (2, 4), and its rows as arrows give (4, 7); times (3, 1) it is (6, 7); times (1, 1) it is (4, 3); times (2, 2) it is (8, 6), with (6, 8) from the rows and (4, 3) from each column once; (1, 2) hits (7, 4) and (3, 2) hits (9, 8); [6 −2; −2 6] times (2.5, 1.5) is (12, 4), with (15, 9) and (18, 14) from the slips

Each puzzle's answer comes from its grid by the rule (the entry row first, the chain's landing point, row 2 and column 2, the rows aimed at the target, rows then columns, the loop voltages), and each slip offered is the one its hint names
Each puzzle offers three different answers, accepts only the right one, and draws every wrong one in the warning colour
Before Check, no puzzle shows its answer (no lit entry, no filled grid, no chain, no landing point); after a right answer, it does

The picture follows the rule: one arrow per lot, each a copy of its column, the last nose on the dot and the answer column at the same point, from none of each to three of each; a lit row reads its across or up parts; a dragged tip rewrites its column; and only one lot of column 1 with two of column 2 hits (7, 4)
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
